Since some people in my household work off-farm, I will keep management simple and practical rather than labor-heavy. For winter wheat, I will use improved seed, do rotary tillage, apply a moderate amount of nitrogen with balanced phosphorus and some potassium, irrigate a few times at the key stages, and spray a couple of times for weeds and disease. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed because it gives me stronger yield on small land, keep fertilizer a bit higher on nitrogen, irrigate in the main water-demand periods, and control pests with a few sprays. I will aim for stable production instead of chasing the highest possible yield, because with only 4.1 mu I care more about reducing risk and making sure the crop succeeds under my household labor situation.
